page: Microsoft Azure F32als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Falsv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks highlight the strong processing capabilities of this hardware configuration. In single-core stress-ng testing, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression, the server achieves top-tier performance within the top 10% of its class. Multi-core stress-ng benchmarks and PassMark CPU scores place the instance in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached and large uncached blocks also demonstrate strong performance, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache.

For specialized workloads, the processor's support for advanced vector extensions (AVX, AVX-512, AVX-VNNI) and cryptography instructions (AES, SHA-NI) enables efficient execution of mathematical and secure operations. Database operations and small-model LLM inference benchmarks rank in the top 10%, while medium-model LLM inference remains strong. The low memory-to-CPU ratio makes this instance a highly cost-efficient choice for compute-bound tasks that do not demand massive memory footprints, such as web serving, batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
